title: Generative AI
definition: AI that makes new things, like writing, images, music or video.
think: The difference between a spam filter and a ghostwriter.

title: Prompt
definition: Whatever you type or say to the AI. The best ones read like a text to a smart friend who knows nothing about your life.
think: Ordering "food, please" vs. "the salmon, sauce on the side."

title: LLM
definition: The engine inside ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini. It read a huge chunk of the internet and learned to guess the next word.
think: Autocomplete that read the whole library.

title: Model vs. app
definition: OpenAI is the company. GPT-6 Astra is one of its models. ChatGPT is the app you open.
think: Toyota, the engine and the Prius.

title: Hallucination
definition: When AI makes something up with a straight face, like a quote nobody said or a study that doesn't exist.
think: The friend who'd rather invent an answer than say "I don't know."

title: Multimodal
definition: AI that understands more than text. Send it a photo or a voice memo.
think: Snap a photo of your fridge and ask what's for dinner.

title: Memory
definition: The app remembering things about you between chats, like your job or that you're vegetarian. You can edit it in settings.
think: A barista who knows your usual.

title: Custom instructions
definition: Notes the AI reads before every chat, like "keep it short" or "I run a nonprofit."
think: The note on the fridge for the babysitter.

title: Projects
definition: A folder for one ongoing thing, with its own chats, files and instructions, so you never re-explain the backstory.
think: Giving your AI its own desk.

title: Model sizes
definition: Most AI companies sell a few sizes. Bigger is smarter, smaller is faster and cheaper. OpenAI's are Astra, Sol and Luna.
think: Coffee sizes. Not every question needs a venti.

title: Training
definition: How a model learns. It reads a mountain of text over and over until the patterns stick.
think: Years of reading before the first day on the job.

title: Knowledge cutoff
definition: The date a model's built-in knowledge stops. Ask about anything newer and it's guessing, unless it can search the web.
think: A smart friend back from six months off the grid.

title: AI slop
definition: The bland, over-polished writing AI churns out when nobody edits it. "I hope this finds you well," forever.
think: Elevator music, but for words.

title: Sycophancy
definition: When AI tells you what you want to hear, like calling your so-so business plan brilliant.
think: A yes-man with a big vocabulary.

title: Deepfake
definition: Fake but real-looking video, audio or photos of a real person. Voice clones make scam calls sound like family.
think: Photoshop, if Photoshop could call your grandma.

title: Token
definition: The bite-size chunks AI reads and writes in, about three quarters of a word each. Prices and limits are counted in them.
think: Gas in the car. Every word in and out burns a little.

title: Context window
definition: How much the AI can hold in its head at once, including your messages, its replies and your files. In long chats, the early stuff starts to slip.
think: A whiteboard. Fill it up and something gets erased.

title: Reasoning model
definition: A model that thinks through a problem before answering. Slower, but much better at math and anything with moving parts.
think: Showing your work instead of blurting out the first number.

title: Deep research
definition: Ask a big question, go make coffee, come back to a report with sources. The AI runs dozens of searches for you.
think: An intern who does the library run for you.

title: Vibe coding
definition: Building an app by describing it in plain English and letting AI write all the code.
think: Telling a builder what house you want and never looking at the blueprints.

title: Agent
definition: AI you give a goal instead of a question. It picks the steps, uses tools like search or your calendar, and keeps going until it's done.
think: Asking for directions vs. handing someone your car keys.

title: Skills
definition: Saved instructions for specific jobs, like your brand rules or how you write a grant. The AI grabs the right one when it needs it.
think: A binder of how-tos a new hire actually reads.

title: Computer use
definition: AI using a computer the way you do, looking at the screen, clicking and typing.
think: Handing someone your laptop and watching over their shoulder.

title: MCP
definition: A standard plug that connects AI to your other apps, like Gmail or Google Drive, so it can get things done there.
think: USB for AI. One plug shape, lots of devices.

title: Prompt injection
definition: Sneaky instructions hidden in a webpage or email that trick AI into doing something you didn't ask for.
think: A note slipped into the to-do pile: "also, wire $500 to this account."

title: Open vs. closed models
definition: Open models, like DeepSeek and Qwen, can be downloaded and run by anyone. Closed ones, like the models in ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, only live behind the company's app.
think: A recipe you can cook at home vs. a dish you can only order at the restaurant.

title: Benchmark
definition: A standardized test for AI. Labs love bragging about scores, and the tests keep getting harder because models keep acing them.
think: The SAT, for robots.

title: GPU
definition: The chips that do AI's heavy math. Nvidia makes most of them, and everyone wants more.
think: Gaming graphics cards that got drafted into a much bigger job.

title: Data center
definition: Warehouses full of those chips, running around the clock. Their power and water use is a big part of the AI debate.
think: The kitchen behind every AI answer.

title: RAG
definition: AI that checks your documents before answering, so it can cite sources instead of going from memory.
think: An open-book test instead of a closed-book one.

title: Fine-tuning
definition: Extra training on a focused set of examples so a model gets great at one job, like writing in your company's voice.
think: A residency after med school.

title: Scaling laws
definition: The pattern that models get smarter as they get bigger and train on more data with more chips. Whether it keeps holding is the trillion-dollar question.
think: Adding horsepower to a car. Works great, until it doesn't.

title: Alignment
definition: Getting AI to do what people actually want, without cutting corners or causing harm. It matters more as models get smarter.
think: Raising a kid who'll end up smarter than you.

title: AGI
definition: AI that can do pretty much any thinking job a person can. Nobody agrees on the definition or when it arrives.
think: A finish line everyone's racing toward, but each team drew it somewhere else.

title: Superintelligence
definition: AI that beats the best humans at nearly everything. The step after AGI.
think: The student who passes the teacher and keeps going.
